purpose: One line per must[] clause of every ACCEPTED epic, naming the artifact that makes it true. Created by the retroactive audit BLOCKED-100 required, and doubling as the standing artifact BLOCKED-101's third pre-flight question produces: a clause with no subject becomes a visible empty row rather than a question nobody asked.

method.question: Does this clause's subject exist in code? NOT whether it is correct or sufficiently tested -- those were signed off already.
method.readNotCount: A keyword hit is not evidence. P4-09's must[2] would have passed a careless grep: `detach` had 5 hits, in the right package, with the right word -- and every one was `detachInputSignal`, an event listener. Each row below was settled by reading the hit, and several probes that returned ZERO turned out to be wrong probes rather than missing subjects (P0-01 must[3], P0-07 must[0], P0-08 must[1], P1-07 must[1], P2-01 must[2]).
method.scope: 72 must[] clauses across 19 ACCEPTED epics. All 19 already have a non-empty acceptance-coverage entry per acceptance clause, verified mechanically.

findings.text: 外部 idempotency ledger 拒绝 stale epoch
findings.verdict: NO SUBJECT -- and worse than absent (sharpened 2026-09-06)
findings.evidence: `idempotencyLedger` and `idempotency ledger` occur 0 times anywhere in packages/. What P4-07 delivers is `checkFencing`, which refuses a token whose epoch is not the item's current one -- a LEASE-level authority check. An idempotency ledger answers a different question: 'have I already applied this effect?'. The nearest thing in the repository is P4-06's message-bus dedup, which belongs to another epic and is not consulted here.
findings.whyItWasMissed: must[0], must[1] and must[2] are all lease/heartbeat/fencing and were built together; must[3] names a component OUTSIDE that cluster. No declared file pointed at it, so neither pre-flight question reached it -- exactly BLOCKED-101's blind spot, in an epic already ACCEPTED.
findings.status: P4-07 is ACCEPTED. Reported for a maintainer decision; not silently reopened.
findings.sharpenedByDelegate: My report said 'idempotency ledger' occurs 0 times, which is true and insufficient -- a mechanism's NAME is not the only evidence of its existence, the trap I had just caught five times in this same audit. Searching by concept instead: `IdempotencyKey` appears 14 times and `idempotencyKey` 18. But following them settles it the other way: both live ONLY in packages/action/action-manifest -- declared in types.ts, computed in canonicalize.ts, exercised by that package's own test. NO consumer anywhere. The key is minted and canonicalized; nothing ever uses it to REFUSE a replay.
findings.whyThisIsWorseThanEmpty: An absent mechanism is honest. Here the system mints idempotency keys, so a future reader finds an `IdempotencyKey` type and a canonicalizer and reasonably concludes deduplication is wired. Identical to P4-09's nesting: machinery present, types present, no call site -- and the part that exists is precisely enough to mislead. Third occurrence of this shape in one session.

findings.text: 将协议 schema 生成物纳入 release evidence 和 golden compatibility fixtures
findings.evidence: The real gap is narrower and harder: EVERY assertion is RELATIVE -- a fingerprint compared against another fingerprint -- and none is ABSOLUTE. Verified: zero 64-hex literals in packages/sdk/protocol/src or /tests. So the suite catches 'this surface differs from that one' and cannot catch 'the ALGORITHM changed', which is the single thing a golden fixture exists for and exactly what must[4] asks for. The release-evidence half is separately absent: `schema` occurs 0 times in scripts/release/collect-evidence.mjs (341 lines), so no protocol schema artifact enters an evidence package.
findings.secondaryFinding: The self-equality assertion is BLOCKED-098's shape: it executes, reports as covered, and can never distinguish any two implementations.
findings.status: P8-01 is ACCEPTED. Reported for a maintainer decision.
findings.correctionToMyOwnReport: My first report called the fingerprint suite BLOCKED-098's shape -- a guard with nothing to decide. THAT WAS WRONG, and wrong in the direction that misdirects the repair. The suite DOES discriminate: reordering a surface keeps the fingerprint (line 149), a version bump changes it (157), an added method changes it (165), a new resource type changes it (169), and moving a name between the method and event kinds changes it (184). A fingerprint function returning a constant would redden four of those. Only line 138's `f(x) === f(x)` is a tautology.
findings.whyTheCorrectionMatters: Read as an 098, the next person deletes line 138 -- a tidy-up that leaves the actual gap untouched. Read correctly, the repair is to ADD a case pinning a fingerprint VALUE. Diagnosis and defect are different things, and I had just written that a false defect 'sends someone to fix what is not broken' -- then produced one, in the diagnosis rather than in the probe.

adopted.name: cedar-policy/cedar
adopted.reason: The authorization engine. Zero runtime dependencies, Apache-2.0, 13.1 MB unpacked, and 4.12.0 is the current latest (published 2026-07-28), so the pin is not stale.

Cedar decides; nothing about how a dsh action becomes a Cedar request exists upstream, and that translation is the clause subject. ledgerRow is null because this is an infrastructure slice, not one of the 109 ledger rows; its card is P2-05's, the first consumer.

adopted.reason: A differential oracle in devDependencies, never a runtime dependency. The hard constraint it documents is reproduced by the frozen case 'canonicalizes at a depth every JS JCS library overflows on, which is why it is hand-written', which asserts this implementation succeeds at depth 5000 where the reference throws.

makeVsUse.residual: The canonicalizer itself, the manifest value-domain refusal, and the manifest-before-execution placement on both dispatch paths. The library decides nothing here; it only says whether the implementation agrees with the standard.

probes.how: frozen case 'canonicalizes at a depth every JS JCS library overflows on, which is why it is hand-written'
probes.evidence: canonicalize@2.1.0: depth 1000 ok, 5000 THREW, 20000 THREW. canonicalize@4.0.0 and json-canonicalize@3.0.0: 5000 THREW. ptc.spec.ts dispatches at depth 5000.

probes.claim: the reference distinguishes NFC from NFD and collapses key order, number spelling and escape spelling
probes.how: frozen case 'produces byte-identical output to `canonicalize` for every generated JSON value' (1000 runs)

gapCheck.gap: src/call-id.ts binds decisions to call ids; not a manifest

makeVsUse.residual: The whole of it. must[0] fixes eight class names, and no external package supplies that vocabulary: the published risk/permission taxonomies are either capability-mechanism lists (what an operation touches) or CVSS-style severity scores for vulnerabilities, and this clause asks for neither. The classifier, its confidence and grounds, its unknown-goes-higher default, and the organisation-policy override are all owned here.

probes.claim: this repository already has a side-effect taxonomy that must[0] could adopt instead of adding a third
probes.evidence: TWO already exist and neither matches. `SideEffectClass` (plugin-manifest/src/types.ts:72) has six values none|read|write|network|process|destructive; `ActionSideEffectClass` (action-manifest/src/types.ts:123) has five, deliberately mirroring the first as a separate type rather than importing it. Both classify MECHANISM (what the operation touches). must[0]'s eight classify RISK (read, local-reversible, internal-write, external-communication, destructive, financial, security-sensitive, safety-critical). They are different axes, so this is a third vocabulary by necessity, not by omission.

probes.claim: the three vocabularies can coexist without a reader conflating them
probes.how: compare the value sets for shared spellings
probes.evidence: `read` and `destructive` appear in all three with different meanings. In action-manifest, `destructive` is additionally the FAIL-CLOSED DEFAULT that classifySideEffect returns when it cannot classify at all. A third `destructive` meaning a risk band is a live conflation hazard, and any mapping between them must be total and monotone or must[1]/acceptance[1] (a plugin cannot downgrade) is unenforceable through the seam.

gapCheck.gap: SideEffectClass is a declared mechanism tag, not a decided risk band; nothing consumes it as policy
ActionSideEffectClass carries the fail-closed default but has no organisation-policy override and no confidence or grounds
presets select a whole policy value for a session; they do not classify an individual action

methodCorrections.lesson: A mechanism's NAME is not the only evidence of its existence.
methodCorrections.detail: I applied 'read, do not count' to five probes that returned ZERO and correctly found the subjects. Then I reported P4-07's absence from a single name search. The delegate searched by CONCEPT and found the type; following it to its consumers is what settled the question -- in the same direction, but for a better reason and with a sharper finding.

methodCorrections.lesson: A wrong diagnosis is a false defect, and false defects send people to fix what is not broken.
methodCorrections.detail: The P8-01 miscall would have produced a deletion instead of an addition. The audit's credibility rests on 2 findings out of 19 rather than 7; a wrong diagnosis damages that the same way a wrong probe would.
